subject: Post-call: technical validation milestones & MAP draft
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@curelytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: technical validation milestones & MAP draft

Daniel / Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a draft MAP milestone for the technical validation so we have shared expectations. Please review and flag any misalignment.

Summary of call
- Goal: validate an LLM-based extract-and-classify capability on Curelytics clinical notes, reaching production-ready latency and unit economics.
- Success criteria discussed: clinically acceptable precision, p95 latency under 450ms for 512-token prompts, and cost below our target per-1k-token threshold.

Draft MAP milestone: Technical validation (owner: Curelytics + Redwood)
1) Test harness & data handoff (target: 2026-07-26)
   - Deliverables: sample dataset (anonymized) + schema; example inference requests; ground truth labels for 1,000 records.
   - Owners: Curelytics: provide data; Redwood (Rishi): test harness and ingestion pipeline.
   - Dependencies: legal signoff on data transfer, SFTP access or Secure Drive.
2) Baseline measurement & smoke benchmarks (target: 2026-08-02)
   - Deliverables: baseline run across 3 candidate models, latency/cost report, failure mode notes.
   - Owners: Redwood: run baselines; Curelytics: provide validation labels.
3) Model shortlist & tuning pass (target: 2026-08-16)
   - Deliverables: shortlist of 2–3 model variants with tuning/quantization plan.
   - Acceptance criteria: recall >= 0.86 on key labels, p95 latency <= 450ms, cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens (at projected throughput).
4) Acceptance run & go/no-go (target: 2026-08-30)
   - Deliverables: final acceptance report, recommended deploy config, rollback plan.

Target close date for MAP: 2026-09-10 (commercial/legal workstream runs in parallel).

Attachments: attached a draft MAP spreadsheet and a short benchmark criteria PDF (filenames below). I left placeholders for test dataset size and owners; Rishi and Ben — can you confirm the runbook steps and any infra prerequisites?

Next steps (requested)
- Daniel: confirm data availability window and anonymization approach by 7/16.
- Curelytics legal: share transfer mechanism preference (SFTP vs. Secure Drive).
- Rishi/Ben: confirm Redwood test harness timeline and required access.

Thanks — I’ll queue a 30-min technical alignment call next week if that helps.

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: curelytics-ma-plan-draft.xlsx (MAP draft workbook), benchmark-slab-criteria.pdf (success criteria primer)

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: technical validation milestones & MAP draft

Thanks Stephanie — this looks constructive. A few quick clarifications inline: 

> 1) Test harness & data handoff (target: 2026-07-26)
>    - Deliverables: sample dataset (anonymized) + schema; example inference requests; ground truth labels for 1,000 records.

We can provide 1,000 labeled records but need to make sure PHI is removed. Our privacy team prefers a hashed ID + date-shifted timestamps. Is that acceptable for the evaluation harness? Also, what format do you need labels in (CSV with label column, or JSONL)?

> 2) Baseline measurement & smoke benchmarks (target: 2026-08-02)

Do you need raw tokens back for debugging, or are redacted summaries sufficient? For initial runs we can provide a debug dump but need an MOU for any verbatim outputs.

> Acceptance criteria: recall >= 0.86 on key labels, p95 latency <= 450ms, cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens

Those look reasonable — can you confirm whether the cost target assumes continuous batching at 8 requests and a 30% cache hit rate? That matters for our procurement numbers.

We’re generally aligned. I can confirm data availability and anonymization approach by 7/16. We’d appreciate a short note on the expected artifact formats so our engineers can prep.

—Daniel

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: technical validation milestones & MAP draft — detailed eval plan

Daniel — thanks for the quick review and good questions. Below is a concise technical evaluation plan that maps to Stephanie's MAP milestones with concrete measurement definitions and owners.

Evaluation plan (owners in parens)
1) Data & artifact formats (Curelytics + Rishi) — due 7/16
   - We expect labels as CSV (id,label_text,confidence_score) and samples as JSONL with fields: id, text, token_count. If Curelytics can provide CSV + JSONL we can onboard quickly.
   - Anonymization: hashed IDs + date-shift acceptable. For any verbatim output storage we'll need a minimal MOU; until then we can store only derived artifacts.
2) Candidate models for baseline (Redwood)
   - Redwood-7B-instruct (fp16), Llama2-13B-chat-8bit, Falcon-40B-instruct-32k (quant eval).
   - Shortlist will be reduced to two variants by 8/16 after a tuning pass.
3) Benchmark success criteria (Redwood + Curelytics)
   - Label-level recall: >= 0.86 across primary labels.
   - Precision: >= 0.80 for any label with prevalence > 5%.
   - Latency: p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 450ms for 512-token prompts measured in our dedicated benchmark harness (no synthetic batching).
   - Cost: <= $0.60 per 1k tokens at projected throughput of 100 simultaneous users and ~8 req/sec aggregate (assumes 30% cache hit).
   - Stability: <1% error rate (timeouts, OOM) in a 10k-request acceptance run.
4) Test sizes and gating (Redwood)
   - Smoke: 1k records across key labels (by 8/02).
   - Acceptance: 10k records for final run (by 8/30).
   - Gating: Acceptance only if all primary criteria are met on the 10k run.
5) Operational checklist (Ben)
   - Access: SFTP or Shared Drive link + temp credentials.
   - Secrets: KMS key required for data-at-rest if using Private deployment.
   - Monitoring: Redwood will provide a trace and token-cost breakdown per run.

Notes on cost assumptions
- The $0.60/1k token target assumes our optimized serving profile: continuous batching for throughput bursts, prefix KV caching for repeated patient contexts, and the quantized model path where applicable. If Curelytics requires strict no-cache evaluation we should adjust the expected cost accordingly.

Drive link to the evaluation runbook (internal view): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_map_technical_eval

Ben and I can take the lead on running the baseline and producing the report. Daniel — if you can confirm data format and the MOU preference (verbatim outputs allowed? limited debug-only?), we’ll lock the dates and push the invite for a 30-min alignment call the week of 7/19.

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

All good to move forward. Quick confirmations: 
- We will provide the 1,000 labeled records by 7/16 as CSV + JSONL with hashed IDs and date-shifted timestamps.
- Curelytics legal prefers Secure Drive for initial transfer; I will share access and a short MOU that allows Redwood to retain derived artifacts but not verbatim clinical text. Expect that by 7/17.
- Regarding caching: we can run two modes — (A) no-cache acceptance run and (B) production-like run with up to 30% cache hit. Please run both so we can see delta for procurement.

Please send a calendar invite for a 30-min alignment next week (7/20–7/23). We’re targeting an internal go/no-go by 9/10 and are aligned on the gating criteria you outlined.

Thanks — looking forward to the baseline report.

—Daniel
